candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether specialty-products revenue is increasingly tied to repair/remodel contractors, insurance-related repairs, regional renovation activity, or landlord maintenance rather than new construction.
candidates.next_evidence: Pull latest 10-K/10-Q customer/end-market disclosure, segment gross margin by specialty vs structural, repair/remodel commentary, inventory turns, branch footprint changes, and management language on 2026 R&R demand.
candidates.node_relation: Distributor of specialty and structural building products with exposure to repair-and-remodel and housing-cycle demand.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Wholesale distributor of residential and commercial building products
candidates.theme_relation: Second-order consumer housing beneficiary: if homeowners, landlords, and contractors repair rather than move, distributors with regional reach and specialty product mix may see demand even when new-home starts are choppy.
candidates.why_include: BlueLinx fits the preferred market-cap hunting zone and sits one layer behind visible retailers/builders as a wholesale distributor of building products. 2025 results identify specialty products as the majority of revenue, making it a plausible repair/remodel and contractor-channel map.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is a small-cap distributor with a messy housing-cycle label, not a clean homebuilder or big-box retailer; market attention may focus on lumber/new-construction cyclicality rather than distribution reach and specialty mix.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether maintenance revenue is more stable than discretionary repair/upgrade and whether branch density creates local distribution leverage when contractors need product availability.
candidates.next_evidence: Track annual report end-market percentages, organic daily sales by category, repair/upgrade vs maintenance trends, irrigation/PVC price effects, contractor customer count, and acquisition-driven branch density.
candidates.node_relation: Distributor to landscape professionals serving maintenance, repair, upgrade, and outdoor-improvement work around residential and commercial properties.
candidates.theme_relation: Adjacent housing-maintenance chokepoint: outdoor maintenance and repair/upgrade spending can persist when households stay in existing homes and landlords maintain rental properties.
candidates.why_include: SiteOne is not a classic housing stock, but its filings identify customers as landscape professionals and disclose a sizable maintenance end market. This makes it a second-order beneficiary of property upkeep and existing-home investment.
candidates.why_underfollowed: The company is often screened as landscaping distribution rather than housing repair/remodel infrastructure, so its link to existing-home maintenance may be under-mapped by consumer-housing screens.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether R&R is a majority or resilient portion of demand, whether dealer channels are gaining share, and whether consolidation with American Woodmark changes customer concentration, pricing power, or integration risk.
candidates.next_evidence: Read latest pro forma filings after the American Woodmark combination, verify repair/remodel vs new-construction exposure, dealer vs builder channel mix, backlog/order trends, and margin impact from cost inflation and integration expenses.
candidates.node_relation: Supplier of residential cabinets used in repair/remodel, kitchen/bath upgrades, and new construction.
candidates.theme_relation: Consumer discretionary housing upgrade exposure: cabinets are a high-ticket product within kitchen/bath remodels, potentially benefiting from homeowners improving existing homes instead of moving.
candidates.why_include: MasterBrand is a direct component supplier into residential remodeling and new construction, but the repair/remodel share and channel mix need tighter validation before treating it as a repair-cycle chokepoint.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Cabinet manufacturers can be buried under broad housing and consumer-durables labels, and cabinet demand may be more tied to dealer/channel dynamics than headline housing starts.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether demand is structurally supported by affordability constraints or merely cyclical; also verify order softness, dealer inventory, product-liability risk, and installation/setup quality issues.
candidates.next_evidence: Compare HUD-code shipment trends, Champion backlog/orders, captive retail contribution, ASP changes, gross margin, warranty/product-liability reserves, and financing availability for manufactured-home buyers.
candidates.node_relation: Manufacturer and retailer of factory-built housing positioned as a lower-cost housing format.
candidates.theme_relation: Affordability-linked consumer housing beneficiary: if site-built housing remains expensive, manufactured homes may capture demand from buyers seeking lower-cost shelter alternatives.
candidates.why_include: Champion Homes directly maps to the affordability part of the node, with recent filings emphasizing factory-built housing and affordable solutions. It is less repair/remodel-specific but relevant to the same housing-affordability pressure.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Manufactured housing can be screened separately from homebuilders and may be missed in standard housing repair/remodel baskets despite being an affordability release valve.

evidence.claim: BlueLinx reported 2025 specialty-products revenue of about $2.053 billion versus total 2025 revenue of about $3.008 billion, indicating that specialty products are the larger revenue category.
evidence.source_title: BlueLinx Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Results

evidence.claim: A 2025 BlueLinx 10-K summary describes the company as a nationwide wholesale distributor focused on residential and commercial building products and notes exposure to housing and repair-and-remodel demand.
evidence.source_title: BlueLinx details specialty shift and Disdero acquisition | BXC Annual Report (10-K)

evidence.claim: SiteOne's 2025 annual report states that customers are primarily residential and commercial landscape professionals, and that approximately 36% of fiscal 2025 net sales related to maintenance.
SiteOne management described expected 2025 end markets as including solid growth in maintenance, which represented about 35% of the business, alongside soft repair and upgrade demand.
evidence.source_title: SiteOne Landscape Supply Announces First Quarter 2025 Earnings

evidence.claim: MasterBrand describes itself as the largest residential cabinet manufacturer in North America and frames repair-and-remodel and new construction as long-term growth markets.
MasterBrand reported full-year 2024 results and noted market headwinds and volume declines, underscoring that cabinet demand remains exposed to housing-cycle volatility.
evidence.source_title: MasterBrand Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2024 Financial Results

evidence.claim: Champion Homes reported fiscal 2025 net sales of $2.5 billion, up 22.7%, driven primarily by the Regional Homes acquisition and higher organic U.S. home sales.
evidence.source_title: Champion Homes Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year Fiscal 2025 Results

evidence.claim: Champion Homes' 2026 10-K summary states the company is focused on expanding products and services that provide more holistic and affordable solutions to homebuyers, and notes HUD-code manufactured housing represented an estimated 10% of 2025 new single-family home starts.
evidence.source_title: Champion Homes Annual Report for Fiscal Year Ending March 28, 2026

memory_update.text: BXC is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the housing repair/remodel node because it is a small-cap wholesale distributor with meaningful specialty building-products exposure; verify true R&R/customer mix before promotion.
SITE is an adjacent-property-maintenance candidate rather than a pure remodel name; maintenance end-market disclosure makes it useful for rental/upkeep mapping.
MBC is a cabinet-component supplier hypothesis for kitchen/bath remodel exposure; requires channel and pro forma merger diligence.
Affordability pressure expands the node beyond repair/remodel into manufactured housing, where SKY is a public pure-play candidate to track alongside repair-cycle suppliers.

Need a later pass on roofing/HVAC/plumbing distributors and restoration-services companies; this pass prioritized listed small/mid-cap names with available public evidence and avoided overfilling with mega-cap retailers.

node: Housing repair, remodel, rental-maintenance, and affordability-linked building products
summary: Layer 1B expands the housing repair/remodel/affordability node away from obvious homebuilders and big-box retailers toward narrower public-market mappings: building-products distribution, landscape-maintenance distribution, residential cabinets, and manufactured housing. The underfollowed angle is that high housing costs and limited mobility may shift wallet share toward maintenance, repair, smaller upgrades, and lower-cost housing formats rather than pure new-site construction. Candidates are research leads only, not recommendations; several still require proof that demand is repair-driven rather than mostly cyclical new construction.
